Although the experience is not perfection itself, there are some very good points that merit five stars.  The food is prepared by a couple older Thai ladies, who use the seasonings and flavor combinations of their homeland.  The proprietor has been in the US for many decades, immigrating when she was young.  Since it is prepared with fresh, local vegetables of the Midwest, the flavors are of course a little different than they would be if prepared with vegetables grown locally in Thailand.  That said, the dishes of rice noodles with peanut sauce, sweet roast chicken, spicy ginger soup, coconut laced salad and fresh fruit for dessert are as authentic as one could ask for.   Of course fluffy white rice was on hand to serve as a base, along with spring rolls and a few unnamed appetizer finger foods.

The eating area is lovingly decorated and comfortable as the pair of older ladies briought out plate after plate of food, until we could eat no more.  Indeed, we took home enough food for several more meals.  The mirrors are kept incredibly clean and polished, creating the illusion of a large yet cozy establishment.  The night we visited there was only one item on the menu: the special.  The special was a multicourse meal, and pay what you want.  These ladies have taken on the task of feeding hungry students from nearby colleges at whatever rate the students can afford.  This is, in itself, remarkable.

I praised their initiative in feeding the hungry and since we're well past the point of pinching pennies in our lives, paid generously for the home cooking and service.  I only hope enough people who are doing well visit Thai Lao with open hearts and open wallets to cover the operating costs of feeding those who are at the beginning of their financial journey.

my girlfriend and I were trying to figure out lunch the other day and she said Thai food. I didn't really want Thai food, like at all. Just being honest I had something similar to Thai food the night before and felt pretty comfortable that I didn't want to eat it. but I also couldn't even in the house I wanted to eat so we just went to get Thai food. walked in and was greeted by the owner, who is very polite, we sat down and tried to figure out what we wanted to eat. My not really wanting Thai food and her not being that hungry made it kind of hard to make a choice. She ended up going with the mango Curry and I got drunken thai noodles.

I can now confidently say that I should probably just always want to eat Thai food anytime it's available. The noodle dish I got, with spice level of 1.5 out of their 1 to 3 scale drama was just about perfect. The noodles were thin and absorbed the awesome not too sweet sauce, there were plenty of vegetables, including a lot of slivered onions which are great. A decent size serving of chicken, andpretty much the perfect spice amount, just enough that I could taste some heat but not enough that it overpowered the other flavors or made me uncomfortable. the owner offered to bring additional spice to the table if I'd like, but I was pretty good without it. My girlfriend's Curry dish was absolutely fantastic, the mango and pineapple added a nice sweetness to the creamy somewhat spiced curry flavor (she got a 1 out of 3), and there was a good mix of both shrimp and chicken, certainly enough for her to have her meal and enough to take home. when it came time for the check she asked for a take-home thing of jasmine rice and they got that out before we were done boxing up our togos.

They only offer dinner size selections on the weekends, and honestly the serving wasn't gigantic the way that I would normally expect from a Thai place at that price point. However the price wasn't that I either, my meal with tip was less than $13, and my girlfriend's, including the extra side of rice to go home was right around $15. perfectly reasonable prices, delicious food, and very friendly service. If you're in the area, or you just want to get some great Thai food go check them out!

Let me start by saying that my wife and I have been looking for decent Asian food and sushi on the south side of Chicago for 3 years and have been disappointed until today..

One of my first impressions came from the lobby where there were multiple comfortable leather lounges, presumably for waiting guests. The lobby was clean and tidy unlike some other local establishments.

The dining area was split into 2 main areas, one of which was set for a large party of about 25 people; the other as more regular booths and tables. There was a short bar, and a fair sized sushi bar with two itame artisans present. We were seated without delay by our host.

The first test of the food was two pieces of tako nigiri and two pieces of maguro nigiri; both were fresh, beautiful, and amply sized. The octopus was not tough and you could taste the subtle flavors, the absence of which for me would have been a disappointment. I also tried the Indie roll (minus the avocado, which I don't palate) for the crispy salmon skin and eel sauce, a delectable treat that balanced the texture of the skin against the sushi and cheese very well. The pickled ginger garnished on the plate was pleasantly piquant and could have been served as a side dish. I would put this sushi on par with some of the better places I've been to around the country. We paired this with a glass of plum wine which had layers and depth of flavor, not the sappy sweet syrup that some places serve.

Next we had the sizzling combo (served on a hot plate) and pineapple fried rice, both of which were delicious and complimented each other well. The portions we're good for 2 - 3 people, with a nice little doggy bag for late night snacking.

The letdown was the dessert choices. I'll be honest, I wasn't expecting much to begin with.. so it was a surprise when the bulk cold staples of chocolate mousse and tiramisu were offset by a creme brulee. Only what came out was NOT creme brulee, just saying. Save your money on that for some ice cream down the street. I will say this, the host cancelled that off the bill without our asking.. good point of service imo.

I took a menu with me as there were quite a few takeout options that we're looking forward to in the Thai and fusion sections. In fact, while we were dining there was a steady flow of pickup orders the entire time. That to me speaks volumes considering the other mediocre choices in the area.

We're going back.. and now that I know this place is here, I believe my wallet is going to suffer in a regular basis 🙂

Now, on to the real star of this place. THE FOOD.

Honestly the best thai food I have had to date. The curry is delicious, some places over power their curry with coconut milk and it becomes sickly sweet. Not at Kim's, curry is amazing, every time period. Definitely my favorite dish there.

The Kim's fried rice and also their volcano dishes also rank among my favorites.

The food WILL be spicy if you ask for it.

Spice level is on a scale of 1 to 10. And can be inconsistent sometimes.

That said a spice level of 5 is way too spicy for me. I typically stay 3 and below to be able to comfortably eat the food with a bit of a kick. For their sweet dishes like the volcano chicken 4 is my max. Rest of the dishes is a 3, for naturally more spicy dishes like the red curry I will get a 2. Other curry I will do a 3.

My Indian coworkers will usually get a range of 5 to 7 for reference.

Sooo KNOW your spice level. Otherwise your dish WILL be spicy. You can get a spice level of 0 so there will not be any spiciness added.

Overall this place is delicous and misunderstood. I don't come here for the great dining experience but the great food.

I personally haven't had any major problems with the owner. But if you don't want to deal with that then I highly suggest ordering food to go.

Exactly the type of friendly, kind service you would expect from Thai people, who are some of the kindest people on earth. They don’t call it the Land of Smiles for nothing!

Amazing Thai food! The food here is the most authentic I’ve had in the Chicagoland area.  We’re talking bamboo shoots and yu choy instead of carrots and gross bell peppers.  I love Thai street food and Immm Rice & Beyond has definitely delivered.  They’re not playing around either, especially keeping with the Thai level spiciness.

They have 2 different menus here, the Rice Accompaniments has the already made food that you can go see up by the front of the restaurant and the regular menu where food is made to order.  Most of the rice accompaniments items are offered in 2 sizes – tasting $5 or family style $9.  They offer sampling of these dishes if you’re worried about the spiciness level.  The tasting portion is a great way to try different dishes.

Tum Yum $8 – This salad was done right with green papaya and level 2 spiciness (you get to pick level 1-4).  It was crunchy and refreshing.
Moo Grob $6 – Crispy pork belly is a fun delicious way to past the time.
Gaeng Tae Poe (Red Curry) $5 – Tamarind red curry with pork belly and water spinach.  Yum!
Gaeng Kiew Whan (Green Curry) $5 – Green curry with bone-in chicken and bamboo shoots and Thai basil. Yum!
Kua Kling $6 – This ground pork in spicy turmeric curry paste is very spicy, but so delicious.
Bamee Moo Hang $10 – OMG, this was to die for.  One of my favorite Thai dishes that is usually a disappointment at other places.  It’s amazing here!  The egg noodles are flavorful and it comes with BBQ pork, bean sprout and yu choy (Chinese leafy green vegetables).
Khao Mun $4 – Aromatic ginger & chicken stock rice.  Delicious and goes well with any dish.
Kanom Jeen $3 – These are round rice noodles that go well with curry dishes.
Kanom Taug $5 – This coconut rice custard is amazing!  It’s creamy and sticky and not too sweet and I can get 10 of these.
Kao Neaw Ma Muong $7 – Mango with sticky rice dessert.  It’s got toasted beans on top!  One of my favorite Thai desserts.

Don’t just go home and leave a bad review they don’t have the opportunity to learn from what’s bothering you and you don’t give them an opportunity to fix it.

The dining experience is not going to be mind blowing. The owner can sometimes be in a good mood and other times bad.

Her English is not the best so I feel sometimes she comes across rude when she is just being blunt. Her humor is a bit dry.

When they are busy she will straight up say they are busy and to come back. Best bet for larger orders is to call it in ahead, especially if planning to dine in. Otherwise I always call mine in to go.

That being said she will bring you out things you need in a timely manner and refill your drinks as needed.

In short, you will be served but not pampered.

Now, on to the real star of this place. THE FOOD.

Honestly the best thai food I have had to date. The curry is delicious, some places over power their curry with coconut milk and it becomes sickly sweet. Not at Kim's, curry is amazing, every time period. Definitely my favorite dish there.

The Kim's fried rice and also their volcano dishes also rank among my favorites.

The food WILL be spicy if you ask for it.

Spice level is on a scale of 1 to 10. And can be inconsistent sometimes.

That said a spice level of 5 is way too spicy for me. I typically stay 3 and below to be able to comfortably eat the food with a bit of a kick. For their sweet dishes like the volcano chicken 4 is my max. Rest of the dishes is a 3, for naturally more spicy dishes like the red curry I will get a 2. Other curry I will do a 3.

My Indian coworkers will usually get a range of 5 to 7 for reference.

Sooo KNOW your spice level. Otherwise your dish WILL be spicy. You can get a spice level of 0 so there will not be any spiciness added.

Overall this place is delicous and misunderstood. I don't come here for the great dining experience but the great food.

I personally haven't had any major problems with the owner. But if you don't want to deal with that then I highly suggest ordering food to go.

The platter had a little of everything and it was all served hot and crispy; I've ordered similar items from other restaurants for delivery/pick-up and now realize that's a mistake when things are deep-fried... eat them right from the source for the best quality.

For the entrees, we had the Lime Chicken which were some of the best breaded chicken bites I've ever eaten (on par with The Village Tavern's breaded chicken tenders). They are drizzled with lime sauce and... oh my... OH... MY... I would demand someone at the table order this every time just so I can have a few bites if I order something else in the future, haha!

The other much-enjoyed entree was the Pad Thai, which remained true-to-heritage with customary ingredients and lots of flavor. I don't recall the Pad Thai tasting of tamarind, which I really am fond of and expect in this dish. Regardless, it was so fresh in terms of veggies and the peanut sauce so delicious, that I was thrilled to have leftovers for a next-day lunch. I just checked the description of their Pad Thai and it says 'egg' in the ingredients, so I'll ask for extra when I choose that entree next time (my Pad Thai entrees can never have enough egg, lol...)

Dessert was some lightly sweetened and very sticky rice with fresh mango slices on top. This was very simple and way too good! I would love more fruit to be served at other restaurants, so Happy Elephant did right with this treat.

Service was great too; we had excellent advice from one of the owners upon arrival (Ning is so nice!) and our server was really on-point with knowing what we needed and providing it almost with premonition-level expertise, lol.

This is another one of those hidden gems I suppose because it's down in the middle of nowhere off of Refugee Road. It sits in a little shopping area called McThai for some reason. The menu was a bit surprising. They actually had real Thai Vietnamese and Chinese dishes. They had bun thit nun! Nobody has that that I found. I probably should have ordered it but I got confused there were so many choices and I wanted to try the Thai food for sure. Maybe Vietnamese next time they even have pho soups! I ordered a bowl of tom ga and it was excellent. Loaded with nice fresh mushrooms big pieces of fish scallions just enough pepper and a nice creamy broth. I ordered a Thai style pork with Thai broccoli and the pork turned out to be something like back bacon and not your usual slices of mystery meat. A nice fatty crust and two layers of fleshy meat cut in cubes so it looks like a layer cake each piece. Actually not too bad at all. Should have ordered it slightly spicier I asked for medium and it was well below the spice threshold for heat. I don't know why they call it broccoli it's more like nice slices of stem cooked just right and leafy parts that more resembled bok choy or spinach. A nice bowl of done properly rice, how many people do Rice properly these days? Ordered a Thai iced tea and even that was correct which is really surprising in Columbus. Only Thai Town in LA or the Thai Beach at Topanga and the Malibu border on Pacific Coast Highway matched this. You get spoiled in places like Los Angeles or New York or overseas where they do food right. This place is worth the drive down to that part of town. When I go back I'm doing the Vietnamese thing.

Short headline: this place has absolutely delicious and authentic Thai food! I lived and worked in Bangkok for 2 years and really appreciate when Thai restaurants in the United States do it correctly, and Thai Thank You really does it super well. When we order Thai, we usually order for dinner and for lunch/dinner the next day. So we ordered 2 orders of Bahmee Wonton, 2 orders of Som Tam Thai, Larb Kai, and 2 sticky rice (which wasn’t on the menu but they were kind enough to add on from the staff’s personal stash), and because our order was over $30, we had a choice of an extra meal so we chose the Pad Thai Kai (chicken). All of it was superb and the prices were better than other Thai restaurants in Chicago.

When I went to the Jits Thai Bistro, the smell was spine-tingling, astonishing! I had to order a to-go lunch. I had the Rotisserie Chicken Fried Rice and the Yellow Curry Chicken w/potatoes and rice and an egg roll. Let me tell you something folks, THAT FRIED RICE IS POSSIBLY THE BEST FRIED RICE TO EVER COME IN CONTACT WITH MY TASTE-BUDS! I could have ate that alone and went away a satisfied customer! The curry was very good, it was a stew like consistency chock full of big chunks of chicken and potatoes. It had a surprisingly pleasant citrus flavor to it. I think it was lime. (I'm no Gordon Ramsey here, I'd fail that blindfold pallet challenge on Hell's Kitchen  without a doubt!) The egg roll had a thin crispy exterior like a spring roll. It was light  and flaky and chock full of flavorful goodness. What made it better was the little cup of sweet and sour sauce that was just enough to pour over the entire length and provide an additional layer of sweet, savory delight!

So of course I had to go again.

The next day I took my step-son. I had the fried rice and egg roll again! This time I changed it up and tried the Spicy Chicken and Basil. Let me tell you something folks, for those of us in the Spencer area who go to restaurants here in town looking for something spicy, you know as well as I do that we are often left wanting... That has changed. Jits Thai Bistro's Spicy Chicken and Basil will LIGHT YOU UP! When I was half way thru this dish, my nose was running and my mouth was on fire! I LOVED IT! I hope it doesn't change! The chicken was moist, the basil flavor added just a hint of anise and licorice flavor and the peppers were just an added bonus to this already delectable dish!

This is a must go to anyone looking for "Something Different" in Spencer. It's about time we had some change in our little town and this place is a much needed breath of fresh air. But you have to get up early to enjoy this treat, as of now (10/08/2015) it's only open Monday - Friday from 11:00 am to 3:00 pm. I hear rumors from the employees though that it's going to open for dinner hours also in a few weeks. I certainly hope so, I got a glimpse of the dinner menu and I would be lying if I said I was not interested in what I saw!

In closing, this is a wonderful place painted in colors that I over heard one of the owners say to a diner, "It's painted those colors to make you hungry." Well sir, you're almost right, it was the smell that came from your front door that made me hungry. Here's to a long successful stay in our small town.

Everything in between classic dishes such as Kun Pao chicken are made at large portions and definitely hit the palette exactly the right way.. The atmosphere is very peaceful. Dim lighting and a lot of cool things to look at. Flaming drinks, shot specials..check the website for more information. It's late night Wednesdays only, it attracts a younger crowd and packs the house just about to capacity every week. With live DJ Matt Aubry to set the mood for a different experience altogether. All and all.. Very very cool place. This is my experience and review. With everything I just mentioned, I think it should probably just about make everybody curious. If you haven't tried this place, it's definitely worth checking out once. Let me tell you a story. Back in 2002 when I was just a promising young teen I would dream of soaring into the stars. I would gaze upon the endless vacuum that is space and wonder if we are truly alone; if we are really God's creation or just a small blue speck in a ocean of space. I needed answers to all of life's questions and I knew only one place could give me the satisfaction that I yearned for. That place is No Thai here in beautiful East Lansing. Within the bustling campus of Michigan State University lives a small island of Thai inspired goodness. Never have I witnessed such grace and care for a restaurant than when I walk through those hallowed doors. A small blanket of happiness and peace engulfs me as arrive and my mood instantly gets better from whatever stress my daily life has bestowed upon me. The food is cooked with the care only compared to a Buddhist monk caring for his temple. The concentration for perfection rivals that of Randy Johnson on the pitchers mound on May 18th, 2004 against the Atlanta Braves. Nothing compares to No Thai. It is my religion, my sanctuary, my release. I am forever grateful for this haven of deliciousness and delight. Thank you.

Although the experience is not perfection itself, there are some very good points that merit five stars.  The food is prepared by a couple older Thai ladies, who use the seasonings and flavor combinations of their homeland.  The proprietor has been in the US for many decades, immigrating when she was young.  Since it is prepared with fresh, local vegetables of the Midwest, the flavors are of course a little different than they would be if prepared with vegetables grown locally in Thailand.  That said, the dishes of rice noodles with peanut sauce, sweet roast chicken, spicy ginger soup, coconut laced salad and fresh fruit for dessert are as authentic as one could ask for.   Of course fluffy white rice was on hand to serve as a base, along with spring rolls and a few unnamed appetizer finger foods.

The eating area is lovingly decorated and comfortable as the pair of older ladies briought out plate after plate of food, until we could eat no more.  Indeed, we took home enough food for several more meals.  The mirrors are kept incredibly clean and polished, creating the illusion of a large yet cozy establishment.  The night we visited there was only one item on the menu: the special.  The special was a multicourse meal, and pay what you want.  These ladies have taken on the task of feeding hungry students from nearby colleges at whatever rate the students can afford.  This is, in itself, remarkable.

I praised their initiative in feeding the hungry and since we're well past the point of pinching pennies in our lives, paid generously for the home cooking and service.  I only hope enough people who are doing well visit Thai Lao with open hearts and open wallets to cover the operating costs of feeding those who are at the beginning of their financial journey.

my girlfriend and I were trying to figure out lunch the other day and she said Thai food. I didn't really want Thai food, like at all. Just being honest I had something similar to Thai food the night before and felt pretty comfortable that I didn't want to eat it. but I also couldn't even in the house I wanted to eat so we just went to get Thai food. walked in and was greeted by the owner, who is very polite, we sat down and tried to figure out what we wanted to eat. My not really wanting Thai food and her not being that hungry made it kind of hard to make a choice. She ended up going with the mango Curry and I got drunken thai noodles.

I can now confidently say that I should probably just always want to eat Thai food anytime it's available. The noodle dish I got, with spice level of 1.5 out of their 1 to 3 scale drama was just about perfect. The noodles were thin and absorbed the awesome not too sweet sauce, there were plenty of vegetables, including a lot of slivered onions which are great. A decent size serving of chicken, andpretty much the perfect spice amount, just enough that I could taste some heat but not enough that it overpowered the other flavors or made me uncomfortable. the owner offered to bring additional spice to the table if I'd like, but I was pretty good without it. My girlfriend's Curry dish was absolutely fantastic, the mango and pineapple added a nice sweetness to the creamy somewhat spiced curry flavor (she got a 1 out of 3), and there was a good mix of both shrimp and chicken, certainly enough for her to have her meal and enough to take home. when it came time for the check she asked for a take-home thing of jasmine rice and they got that out before we were done boxing up our togos.

They only offer dinner size selections on the weekends, and honestly the serving wasn't gigantic the way that I would normally expect from a Thai place at that price point. However the price wasn't that I either, my meal with tip was less than $13, and my girlfriend's, including the extra side of rice to go home was right around $15. perfectly reasonable prices, delicious food, and very friendly service. If you're in the area, or you just want to get some great Thai food go check them out!

What a fantastic restaurant! As soon as I walked in the relaxing, modern ambiance of Nawa was apparent and inviting. The lighting level and the stylish light fixtures set the mood along with some excellent low-level music playing.

Our waiter, Estevan, was highly knowledgeable; he initially gave us some information about the nature of the restaurant and some background on the culinary staff. After giving us a moment to look over the menu, he gave multiple excellent recommendations regarding our desire to find something unique for an appetizer as well as selecting our entrees. He also was very attuned to the way they prepared their food.

The appetizer we had was the "Gyoza Panang" which was a rice-dumpling in their panang sauce that was done to perfection and had plenty of mixed flavors with the inclusion of chicken, lightly seared red pepper slivers, and cabbage.

We thoroughly enjoyed the food as the flavors were bright and unique. My wife had the "Basil Stir Fry" with chicken and she was a big fan of the basil flavor that was evident in the dish that made it very unique. I ordered the "Green Curry" with pork and the bamboo shoots, basil, and eggplant were all welcome and unique additions to the meal. Both dishes were cooked masterfully and each had their own nuances that I wish I had the capacity to describe more in-depth.

Both of our meals were prepared at a moderate level of heat, as was the recommendation of our waiter but was weak enough that my wife didn't mind. Possibly my favorite part of the dining experience was the presence of a set of three ceramic jars to add different amounts of heat to the food. There was a sauce similar to (if not actually) Sriracha sauce, then a chili oil with chili flakes, and then some dry hot chili flakes. I ended up adding quite a lot of each by the time my bowl was empty. Both of our entrees also came with a generous portion of rice as well.

We enjoyed some Thai Iced Coffee during the meal that I had wanted to order a single serving of, but the waiter kindly split the drink for us and seemed to have provided much closer to two full servings for us--and they were delicious indeed! Chocolately notes of coffee mixed mixed with cream made for a tasty and enjoyable compliment to the spiciness of our meals.

At the end of our meal, we were close enough to the bar to grab the attention of the bartender and ask about some mini white oak barrels they had been using to make some signature drinks in. The bartender we spoke to was full of enthusiasm, as he was the one responsible for crafting most of their specialty drinks (which we unfortunately didn't try during our meal). Hopefully next time!

Nawa is making an excellent reputation for themselves in Fort Wayne as a unique and high-end dining experience with reasonable prices and a variety of options for both cautious and adventurous diners alike. We can't wait to have a chance to visit again.

The food was amazing and would give Benihana a run for their money! The other thing that impressed me was that my son and I were sharing a meal and after giving me my portions he continued to cut the chicken (we had the chicken and mushrooms) into smaller bites for him. It's these details that create loyalty and I will definitely be back. Thank you.

Now onto the food. We started off with a mushroom broth soup which was good. The salad was an iceberg lettuce salad with a creamy ginger dressing that felt a little watered down. Good flavor though. Overall the soup and salad was good but not earth shattering. The Hibachi like I said was fantastic. I ordered the chicken hibachi and my wife got the shrimp. We started off with the fried rice which was flavorful and delicious. Next was the noodles. It was a typical wide rice noodle drenched with garlic butter and more butter and a dash of teriyaki and soy sauce. How could it not be good. The veggies were cooked with basic oil and butter but were a perfect balance of tender but crisp. The chicken and shrimp were cooked to perfection and still moist. There was a ton of food to feed us another night... left over hibachi tomorrow night... Yes please! Overall the service and food was awesome so 5 stars. I look forward to coming back and seeing what else they have to offer.

So, I used to hate sushi.  My friends said that it was an acquired taste, that I would get used to the dead fish taste like I got used to beer.  One of the reasons it is, in fact, hard to get an opinion on sushi is that many people have acquired a taste for bad sushi, marked by the fact that it tastes like dead fish.  The Sapporo Wind, the ancestor of The Sapporo Sushi Factory, broke me of my hatred.  Turns out, good sushi doesn't taste like dead fish at all.

So, as I understand it, the owner of the Wind is the owner of the Factory and he is considered one of the best sushi chefs in the world.  The open-faced sushi, by the way, should not be feared.  It is called the Horo Special and it is delicious.  The sushi chef at the Factory is experimental, and that is what sets him above and apart from others. Even his experiments taste like good, traditional sushi at their base.

Having been to at least a dozen different chains including Mr. Sushi and Otani, I have to say that none of them give me that good food hum like the Factory.  Customers are treated well and I like the simplicity and the comfort of the decor.

my girlfriend and I were trying to figure out lunch the other day and she said Thai food. I didn't really want Thai food, like at all. I can now confidently say that I should probably just always want to eat Thai food anytime it's available. The noodle dish I got, with spice level of 1.5 out of their 1 to 3 scale drama was just about perfect. The noodles were thin and absorbed the awesome not too sweet sauce, there were plenty of vegetables, including a lot of slivered onions which are great. A decent size serving of chicken, andpretty much the perfect spice amount, just enough that I could taste some heat but not enough that it overpowered the other flavors or made me uncomfortable. the owner offered to bring additional spice to the table if I'd like, but I was pretty good without it. My girlfriend's Curry dish was absolutely fantastic, the mango and pineapple added a nice sweetness to the creamy somewhat spiced curry flavor (she got a 1 out of 3), and there was a good mix of both shrimp and chicken, certainly enough for her to have her meal and enough to take home. when it came time for the check she asked for a take-home thing of jasmine rice and they got that out before we were done boxing up our togos.

They only offer dinner size selections on the weekends, and honestly the serving wasn't gigantic the way that I would normally expect from a Thai place at that price point. However the price wasn't that I either, my meal with tip was less than $13, and my girlfriend's, including the extra side of rice to go home was right around $15. perfectly reasonable prices, delicious food, and very friendly service. If you're in the area, or you just want to get some great Thai food go check them out!

Let me start by saying that my wife and I have been looking for decent Asian food and sushi on the south side of Chicago for 3 years and have been disappointed until today..

One of my first impressions came from the lobby where there were multiple comfortable leather lounges, presumably for waiting guests. The lobby was clean and tidy unlike some other local establishments.

The dining area was split into 2 main areas, one of which was set for a large party of about 25 people; the other as more regular booths and tables. There was a short bar, and a fair sized sushi bar with two itame artisans present. We were seated without delay by our host.

The first test of the food was two pieces of tako nigiri and two pieces of maguro nigiri; both were fresh, beautiful, and amply sized. The octopus was not tough and you could taste the subtle flavors, the absence of which for me would have been a disappointment. I also tried the Indie roll (minus the avocado, which I don't palate) for the crispy salmon skin and eel sauce, a delectable treat that balanced the texture of the skin against the sushi and cheese very well. The pickled ginger garnished on the plate was pleasantly piquant and could have been served as a side dish. I would put this sushi on par with some of the better places I've been to around the country. We paired this with a glass of plum wine which had layers and depth of flavor, not the sappy sweet syrup that some places serve.

Next we had the sizzling combo (served on a hot plate) and pineapple fried rice, both of which were delicious and complimented each other well. The portions we're good for 2 - 3 people, with a nice little doggy bag for late night snacking.

The letdown was the dessert choices. I'll be honest, I wasn't expecting much to begin with.. so it was a surprise when the bulk cold staples of chocolate mousse and tiramisu were offset by a creme brulee. Only what came out was NOT creme brulee, just saying. Save your money on that for some ice cream down the street. I will say this, the host cancelled that off the bill without our asking.. good point of service imo.

I took a menu with me as there were quite a few takeout options that we're looking forward to in the Thai and fusion sections. In fact, while we were dining there was a steady flow of pickup orders the entire time. That to me speaks volumes considering the other mediocre choices in the area.

We're going back.. and now that I know this place is here, I believe my wallet is going to suffer in a regular basis 🙂

I have been dining at Zab since they opened, having been thrilled that a Thai restaurant opened close by (I have since moved from Loveland to Morrow, but I still order from Zab). I have been to Thai restaurants all over the States and also many, many different countries.

The food is nearly always fresh, consistently well spiced, and delicious. Years ago my first introduction to Thai food was "Bangkok Thai" in Milford, which has since changed names a myriad of times and is probably closed. I was hooked on the first bite and this was at least 15 years ago - yes friends, Thai food is THAT good!

Zab's does nearly all of their dishes well. I have tried many of the dishes on the menu, and unsurprisingly I go for the Pad Thai most of the time (4 out of 5 hot with beef, not chicken, which is unusual but I enjoy it!). I always get a side order of Spring Rolls and I have to say they make the BEST Spring Rolls I have ever had from a Thai restaurant. So fresh, perfectly cooked, great balance, and a tremendously delicious dipping sauce.

I have also had the Basil Noodles which are wonderful (but not a "regular" order for me at least), the Holy Basil, the Braised Pork, and finally - and possibly one of their best dishes - the Massaman Curry. I have never been disappointed with the food whatsoever, but of course some dishes are better than others. There is a reason they list things like the Massaman Curry under "Specialties" - because they know how to make it very damn well!

All in all, an unassuming but delicious restaurant that has been around long enough now to have made a name for itself. Yes, it's in a strip mall. Yes, most people would assume it would be "meh" and just barely acceptable. But that ain't the truth folks - this place is a gem, a diamond in the rough. Strip mall and preconceived notions be damned; this is a genuine five star Thai restaurant.

We also had Fresh rolls (meat, cilantro and lettuce wrapped in rice paper) which were very refreshing (not at all savory and must be eaten with the accompanying sauce for more flavor). So I found this hidden gem on accident. Was going for movie with mom and aunt at AMC Barrington. We were late for the 6:30 show so we said let's go to 9:20 show and eat first. The daughter was serving basically all the tables and running the register and I believe the Mom was cooking. One man came later to drop off a dish from the back but not sure if it was the brother. So we ordered drinks and I wanted a beer which they don't serve alcohol so I ordered a Thai Iced Tea (pretty good... tasted like most other places). Then we ordered veggie egg rolls, edamame and small cucumber salad (enough for three but could have had a large cause it was so good but because we were ordering more food we didn't want to fill up plus we weren't sure how it would taste but now I think I would have ordered the large and ate some more because it was light dish). Egg rolls were crispy and tasty and edamame was warm and salty and crispy (maybe could be cooked for another minute but that perhaps would have lost its crunch but it was tasty... it's edamame can't do much with it). The cucumber salad was super tasty. The vinaigrette dressing on it was so good. We added mixed some of the Thai chilli sauce we had with the egg Roz for a little kick. So tasty! I'm not veg but my mom and aunt are so I decided to order all veg dishes so we could all share. Great idea because everything I ate was hella good. For our main entrees basil fried rice at the recommendation of the server she if we wanted tofu or vegetable. So my mom isn't a tofu fan but my aunt and I do eat it so we ordered vegetable and basically they add more and different veggies than what's in the base dish. I'm glad we did. So damn delicious! We also ordered the Panang curry let her recommendation and it was light and tasty and ordered with vegetable also instead of tofu and that was also a good idea because it had more veggies in addition to the base. Lastly we ordered crazy noodles but with tofu this time instead of additional veggies because I thought would be good to have at least one dish with tofu and that's what server recommended also. It was made to perfection. The tofu was nice and crispy not soft like some places and noodles and veggies were great combo with it. All three main dishes were so good and we did hot and medium hot for dishes as we like spicy. You won't die from heat it was good flavor and my aunt can't eat too hot and she enjoyed it. So we ate with the spicy Thai chilli sauce and some left over sweet and sour sauce we had with egg rolls. The combination of the three dishes was amazing which I let the server know several times. Poor girl seemed overwhelmed a tiny bit handling all the tables (I think there are like 10 and they were more than 2/3 full) but she was nice and didn't complain and melt smiling even when we asked for more sauce and napkins. I asked her as o was paying bill it was family owned and she said yes. It's been open for ten years. We live in Wheaton near Naperville and cane to Barrington area just for movie so this isn't close for us however I would drive all the way again just to eat here as I loved it so much! If you are familiar with thai food already, you will like or love the food. It is not overly altered for the American Pallette. For appetizers, The Tom Yam Guy (hot and sour Thai style, not Chinese) and Tom kha guy (Tom yam with coconut milk) were both so flavorful, comforting and delicious. We also had Fresh rolls (meat, cilantro and lettuce wrapped in rice paper) which were very refreshing (not at all savory and must be eaten with the accompanying sauce for more flavor). The shrimp curry was a thin coconut milk style and incredibly savory; spiced and seasoned well. It has a nice kick to it; I ordered spicy but they have mild and medium options as well. The pad Thai was not too sweet or bland as I have experienced at other places; the flavors were well balanced, layered well and incredibly delicious and savory. I will be returning! The other much-enjoyed entree was the Pad Thai, which remained true-to-heritage with customary ingredients and lots of flavor. I don't recall the Pad Thai tasting of tamarind, which I really am fond of and expect in this dish. Regardless, it was so fresh in terms of veggies and the peanut sauce so delicious, that I was thrilled to have leftovers for a next-day lunch. I just checked the description of their Pad Thai and it says 'egg' in the ingredients, so I'll ask for extra when I choose that entree next time (my Pad Thai entrees can never have enough egg, lol...)

Dessert was some lightly sweetened and very sticky rice with fresh mango slices on top. This was very simple and way too good! I would love more fruit to be served at other restaurants, so Happy Elephant did right with this treat.

Service was great too; we had excellent advice from one of the owners upon arrival (Ning is so nice!) and our server was really on-point with knowing what we needed and providing it almost with premonition-level expertise, lol.

The beef salad has the fish sauce and hints of mint with lime and the sometum is the best I have had outside of when my sweetheart or I make it at home.  Even a simple dish like Spicy Fried Rice left a remarkable impression upon my palate!  If you can make fried rice memorable, you got talent.
Lastly, while I know this really isn't important to some, I feel I must mention that their ice tea is really some of the best I have had in years.  Not the "thai ice tea" or sweet tea, just their plain old ice tea.  They brew it very well.  So much better than what you get in many commercialized restaurant settings.  More like what you would find in a small town diner that does things like tea the old fashioned way.
After all, it is the little things that count.

What a fantastic restaurant! As soon as I walked in the relaxing, modern ambiance of Nawa was apparent and inviting. The lighting level and the stylish light fixtures set the mood along with some excellent low-level music playing.

Our waiter, Estevan, was highly knowledgeable; he initially gave us some information about the nature of the restaurant and some background on the culinary staff. After giving us a moment to look over the menu, he gave multiple excellent recommendations regarding our desire to find something unique for an appetizer as well as selecting our entrees. He also was very attuned to the way they prepared their food.

The appetizer we had was the "Gyoza Panang" which was a rice-dumpling in their panang sauce that was done to perfection and had plenty of mixed flavors with the inclusion of chicken, lightly seared red pepper slivers, and cabbage.

We thoroughly enjoyed the food as the flavors were bright and unique. My wife had the "Basil Stir Fry" with chicken and she was a big fan of the basil flavor that was evident in the dish that made it very unique. I ordered the "Green Curry" with pork and the bamboo shoots, basil, and eggplant were all welcome and unique additions to the meal. Both dishes were cooked masterfully and each had their own nuances that I wish I had the capacity to describe more in-depth.

Both of our meals were prepared at a moderate level of heat, as was the recommendation of our waiter but was weak enough that my wife didn't mind. Possibly my favorite part of the dining experience was the presence of a set of three ceramic jars to add different amounts of heat to the food. There was a sauce similar to (if not actually) Sriracha sauce, then a chili oil with chili flakes, and then some dry hot chili flakes. I ended up adding quite a lot of each by the time my bowl was empty. Both of our entrees also came with a generous portion of rice as well.

We enjoyed some Thai Iced Coffee during the meal that I had wanted to order a single serving of, but the waiter kindly split the drink for us and seemed to have provided much closer to two full servings for us--and they were delicious indeed! Chocolately notes of coffee mixed mixed with cream made for a tasty and enjoyable compliment to the spiciness of our meals.

At the end of our meal, we were close enough to the bar to grab the attention of the bartender and ask about some mini white oak barrels they had been using to make some signature drinks in. The bartender we spoke to was full of enthusiasm, as he was the one responsible for crafting most of their specialty drinks (which we unfortunately didn't try during our meal). Hopefully next time!

Nawa is making an excellent reputation for themselves in Fort Wayne as a unique and high-end dining experience with reasonable prices and a variety of options for both cautious and adventurous diners alike. We can't wait to have a chance to visit again.

Ever since Thai Palace closed since years back, I've been looking for a good, local Thai food diner for the occasional carryout fix. Lue Thai fits the bill.

I won't confess to being very adventurous when it comes to Thai cuisine, but I could eat Pad Thai every other day, and theirs is delicious. Sadly, I'm not so young anymore, and can't handle the hottest spice levels that I would prefer in my Pad Thai, but their medium level I think is perfect for the average diner. The portions are generous, and they don't skimp on the proteins. Chicken Pad Thai is LOADED with chicken. One order is easily enough for dinner and lunch the next day.

On occasion, I'll also get the Pad See Ew, which is a wide noodle with a savory dark soy sauce that's kind of tangy and a bit sweet, stir fried with egg and broccoli. The sauce can be pretty salty, but it's generally really good. The broccoli is always perfectly firm and never mushy.

One slight disappointment I'll note is Chicken Satay. While the flavors are great, and the peanut and cucumber sauces that are included are also good, everytime I've ordered it,  it seems the chicken is a always a bit overcooked,and not as juicy as it should be.

I got my bowl nice and full but I do miss the explanation on the glass of what each item was, I do know my veggies but when you have 3 different mushroom, I’d like to know what is what. We've been to Big Bowl several times, most recently today for lunch. We waited a few minutes for a table which was expected because they were fairly busy. We were seated at a table by the window and it was a nice sunny day for February.

I started with a bowl of Hot and Sour soup. Big Bowl has the most delicious hot and sour soup I've had anywhere. I've had it at many restaurants.

For my entree I had the stir fry bar. Now they have a large menu so they have lots of great looking entrees to choose from, but for me the stir fry is the way I like to go. You get to go up and pick out your exact vegetables yourself. You get a clean bowl, and a clean pair of tongs and you go along and put your vegetables you want into your bowl. They have tons of choices to choose from including bok choy, bean sprouts, water chestnuts, baby corn, regular corn, peas, edamame, onions, white mushrooms, 2 other kinds of Asian mushrooms, broccoli, snow peas, bamboo shoots, green peppers, zucchini, jalapeno peppers, Anaheim peppers and habanero peppers. I've probably forgotten a few items but those are most of the choices. For the stir fry you also pick your protein (or no protein), choice of different noodles or rices, and choice of sauce. It's a really great setup you get to pick every component. It is always delicious. Today I picked my vegetables, no protein, Kung Pao sauce with peanuts and Chow Fun noodles (thick Asian noodles).

My wife had the Ahi Tuna Poke Bowl and really enjoyed the freshness of it.

My only complaint would be that our entrees were brought to the table after I had only had my soup for about 2 minutes. So I had to decide whether to let my soup get  cold and eat my entree or to finish my soup and let my entree get cold. I chose to eat my entree and let my soup get cold.

We highly recommend Big Bowl and hope you give it a try.

My favorite Pad Thai in Wisconsin comes from a small place in Milwaukee.  I dont want to drive all the way there every time I want Pad Thai, so I've been looking for a place in Madison that I like almost as much.  I searched Google and Yelp for "best Pad Thai".  Amongst all of the popular, mainstream places I've already tried I spotted Hot-n-Spicy.  It was a couple miles from my house and closed early, but was still open at the time I searched.  Seemed like it was meant to be.

It's tucked away in back of a decidedly nonglamorous Asian grocer.  The restaurant is even less glamorous-- a cluttered kitchen partitioned off but visible, a few well worn tables.  It's probably very clean but looks dirty.  Certain people might be put off, but I know these type of places often have the very best food.

I placed my usual order-- Pad Thai with chicken, medium spice-- and asked if there was anything else I NEEDED to try.  They said, their egg rolls are better than anywhere else.  So I ordered them as well.

The egg rolls are small, and definitely some of the best I've had.  They remind me of homemade egg rolls from Asian friends of my childhood.  I've very glad I got them.

The Pad Thai.  Well.  I dont like my food super hot, but I can tolerate more spice than most (white and/or American) people.  I'm not entering any hot wing or hot pepper challenges, but I use lots of hot sauce, and it's rare that anything on an American restaurant menu is too hot for me.  Everywhere I get Pad Thai, I ask for medium spice, which sometimes is still too mild (Sa-Bai Thong for example), other times it's just the perfect amount of bite.  This time.  Well.  It took me two glasses of milk to get through the whole bowl.  It wasnt curled up in a ball on the floor, Tom Haverford "This is how you eaaatttt ittt!!!!" hot, but it was hot enough where the spice eclipsed the flavor, which is too hot for me.  I get that the name is Hot-n-Spicy, but I still thought medium would be medium.

Also, there was very little chicken in my bowl.  If I try it again, I'm going to ask for mild, and for extra chicken.

We tried Amazing Myanmar Asian Cuisine today. The owners were super friendly and welcoming. I would first warn everyone that this is an authentic tasting place. Anyone looking for Americanized food that other restaurants serve would probably be disappointed. The deep fried spring rolls were tasty. The tea leaf salad was very interesting. I loved the flavor, but the mixture of crunchy and soft textures may be odd for some people. The mohinga noodle soup was very tasty, but a little on the fishy side so it's not for everyone. It reminds me of a Vietnamese noodle soup called bun rieu. The Myanmar coconut curry noodles were delicious. I think anyone who likes coconut curry would like that dish. The pad thai was a bit different than what you normally get at Thai restaurants in that it was not super flavorful. We got it for the kids so we made it not spicy, but I think it had potential to be really good with some added spice. My favorite dish was the steamed fish. The spicy lime sauce that it came in was to die for and the fish itself was so tender and delicious. This is another authentic style dish where you have to pick out the bones a bit so not recommended for children, but it was totally worth it. For dessert, we were given sweet sticky rice. It was really good and not overly sweet like at some other places. My only negative is the sushi. It's not that the sushi was bad, but it just wasn't anything special. I don't think it really blends in with their menu that well. I would love to come back and try more dishes. Overall, I'd give them 4/5 because of authenticity and service.

Ever since Thai Palace closed since years back, I've been looking for a good, local Thai food diner for the occasional carryout fix. Lue Thai fits the bill.

I won't confess to being very adventurous when it comes to Thai cuisine, but I could eat Pad Thai every other day, and theirs is delicious. Sadly, I'm not so young anymore, and can't handle the hottest spice levels that I would prefer in my Pad Thai, but their medium level I think is perfect for the average diner. The portions are generous, and they don't skimp on the proteins. Chicken Pad Thai is LOADED with chicken. One order is easily enough for dinner and lunch the next day.

On occasion, I'll also get the Pad See Ew, which is a wide noodle with a savory dark soy sauce that's kind of tangy and a bit sweet, stir fried with egg and broccoli. The sauce can be pretty salty, but it's generally really good. The broccoli is always perfectly firm and never mushy.

One slight disappointment I'll note is Chicken Satay. While the flavors are great, and the peanut and cucumber sauces that are included are also good, everytime I've ordered it,  it seems the chicken is a always a bit overcooked,and not as juicy as it should be.

Staff is really friendly and pleasant, and the restaurant clean and comfortable. We tried Amazing Myanmar Asian Cuisine today. The owners were super friendly and welcoming. I would first warn everyone that this is an authentic tasting place. Anyone looking for Americanized food that other restaurants serve would probably be disappointed. The deep fried spring rolls were tasty. The tea leaf salad was very interesting. I loved the flavor, but the mixture of crunchy and soft textures may be odd for some people. The mohinga noodle soup was very tasty, but a little on the fishy side so it's not for everyone. It reminds me of a Vietnamese noodle soup called bun rieu. The Myanmar coconut curry noodles were delicious. I think anyone who likes coconut curry would like that dish. The pad thai was a bit different than what you normally get at Thai restaurants in that it was not super flavorful. We got it for the kids so we made it not spicy, but I think it had potential to be really good with some added spice. My favorite dish was the steamed fish. The spicy lime sauce that it came in was to die for and the fish itself was so tender and delicious. This is another authentic style dish where you have to pick out the bones a bit so not recommended for children, but it was totally worth it. For dessert, we were given sweet sticky rice. It was really good and not overly sweet like at some other places. My only negative is the sushi. It's not that the sushi was bad, but it just wasn't anything special. I don't think it really blends in with their menu that well. I would love to come back and try more dishes. Overall, I'd give them 4/5 because of authenticity and service.

When we walked in, we were greeted by a friendly hostess who also happened to be our server.  She allowed us to sit wherever we like.  We chose a booth near the entrance.  The first thing I noticed as I sat was that the seat had lost some of its cushion (I could feel the wood frame through it) - I am guessing the furniture is just old.  I also noticed that the carpet all around the restaurant was very old and in bad shape, showing the traffic lanes between tables; it really needs to be replaced.

She promptly asked us for our drink orders.  I got the Vietnamese iced coffee, and this was immediately a hit with me... perfectly sweet, perfectly strong, and served in a nice, big glass.

We both got sushi rolls and I also ordered some of the crab fried rice.  The sushi was very good, and it came out super quickly.  My roll was called the Rock & Roll, which was tempura battered and fried before being cut and served... it might be one of my favorite rolls ever, really impressive.

My fried rice came out before I was even finished with my sushi... the kitchen was on it!  I consider myself a fried rice connoisseur, so I was prepared to really judge them on it (much like how fries can be a good barometer for an American restaurant, it is my opinion that fried rice can be that for east Asian restaurants).  I finished my sushi before digging into the rice.  From the first bite, I was really pleased with the flavor!  The jasmine rice was still fragrant and very comforting.  However, there were a couple things I did notice about it that could be better.  This particular dish included pineapple, but I am fairly certain they used canned pineapples and didn't cook them at all; it would have been much better to grill fresh pineapple and toss that in.  Also, the menu specified the dish was made with lump crab meat, but this was not the case... they used imitation crab (could tell by how it had the shredded texture).  Now, to be fair, I did really enjoy the fried rice and I finished the whole thing - I even enjoy imitation crab; but if the menu specified lump crab meat, it should have been real crab.

So, we left full and happy.  The sushi especially was really impressive and reasonably priced.  There are some needed improvements as I suggested above... they really should update the furniture and flooring, and take to heart my feedback on the fried rice.  But don't mistake my constructive criticism for bashing - it was an all-around good experience and we will be back!

This place is advertised as "vegetarian friendly".  We were disappointed that both soups had chicken in them; but our friendly and helpful waitress told us the Tom Yum soup could be made without the ubiquitous bird.  The soup was spicy and flavorful.  I ordered a dish with white rice and veggies with well browned tofu.  My wife ordered a noodle dish.  You can order mild, medium, or hot.   Having learned caution earlier in life, we chose medium.  It had a good heat to it, but next time we will order hot.  The "crab" rangoon and veggie eggrolls were perfect appetizers.  They were really good.  The portions of our meals were prodigious. I would suggest that if you have appetizers, you split an entree. Otherwise you will be eating your order for the next day. The lass waiting on us was perky and really seemed like she wanted us to have a good experience.  The food was very tasty; and we enjoyed our meals quite a bit.  Both of us are very sensitive to MSG.  My wife thought she had a mild reaction.  I didn't.  So I will ask them, point blank, next time we go here.

If you have not been to Big Bowl or a restaurant like it, you get into a line, grab a bowl, and select your vegetables. The server took care of it right away - made sure he took my order again, made sure we were not double-charged, and I had the food remade. When it came out this time, it was right. For the past couple years, I've been coming to Phaya Thai once every few weeks because it's a convenient stop on the way home from work, and because there aren't very many decent Thai places on the east side of town. What prompted my review tonight, however, was an experience that has has left an indelible impression on me.  I called in an order for myself and my wife (two entrees and an appetizer) and was told that it would be ready in 15 minutes.  I arrived 15 minutes later and paid, and then over the next 25 minutes, I watched a dozen orders prepared and given to people who arrived after me (after waiting 20 minutes, the polite hostess assured me that mine was next up, and three more orders went out before my food was finally ready).

This all would have been a minor inconvenience if the food had been as tasty as it normally is, but the drunken noodles were so overcooked that they had a texture that my wife likened to snot (drunken noodles are one of our favorite dishes, and these were the worst we've ever had).  The pad thai was pretty good, though, so we were at least able to split that.

As a result, we were constantly keeping an eye on the clock, which personally speaking, doesn't make it much of an enjoyable dining experience if you feel like you're being rushed every step away.

Ironically, the only thing not rushed about the experience was the service itself. Despite having ordered within the first 15 minutes, we only received our first appetizer 20 minutes later and that's without any wine, since that was brought to us afterwards. Food was brought out nearly an hour in, and thankfully it actually tasted good and is the only reason besides the interior why I'm giving it a three stars. We ordered a variety of sushi rolls, filet mignon, and one of the pastas with shrimp. Sushi was fresh but bland and the pasta and filet mignon were absolutely mouthwatering. However, the highlight for me was the chocolate cake dessert served with ice cream; it was one of the best tasting desserts I've had.

Unfortunately, those pleasant moments were bittersweet ones with everything being rushed. We barely had enough time to finish everything and with staff members constantly trying to take plates with food away, it became irritating. Maybe if everything were brought out faster, the atmosphere would have been different but with such time limitations and with the overall pace of things, I would only recommend this place for cocktails, appetizers, and dessert.

Number one, whenever you order something for take-out that includes rice, they will consistently give you major empty space at the top of the rice box. We had high hopes when we went to this place for dinner, but the food was middling--not great, not terrible. The crab rangoons were fine and properly done (for crab rangoons, at least), but the pan-fried pork dumplings were limp and bland. The General Tso's Chicken was the best entree of the four we tried: the chicken pieces were large and meaty with just enough breading; the sauce was okay--a standard goopy, semi-sweet, uncomplicated sauce. The orange beef was several small cutlets of flattened beef fried in a standard breading with a sweet, goopy, one-dimensional sauce that faintly tasted of orange. It was fine enough for this sort of thing, but it didn't have the zing and spice that more complex versions (those with orange peel, ginger chunks, etc.) tend to have. The Beef Rendang, an Indonesian specialty, was tasty, but it was just several chunks of beef and potato in a Rendang-flavored sauce. In better versions of this dish, the ingredients cook together for a long time to yield slightly caramelized beef and potatoes in a highly flavorful, concentrated sauce. The Thai green curry had lots of green and non-green veggies in it, but the pork was the very thinly sliced, highly processed "BBQ style" pork you find in some Chinese soups, and the green curry sauce was very thin and not very flavorful. The staff were very nice and obliging, though, and it seems to be a popular spot with some locals, so you may as well try it for yourself and see if you like it.

We had high hopes when we went to this place for dinner, but the food was middling--not great, not terrible. The crab rangoons were fine and properly done (for crab rangoons, at least), but the pan-fried pork dumplings were limp and bland. The General Tso's Chicken was the best entree of the four we tried: the chicken pieces were large and meaty with just enough breading; the sauce was okay--a standard goopy, semi-sweet, uncomplicated sauce. The orange beef was several small cutlets of flattened beef fried in a standard breading with a sweet, goopy, one-dimensional sauce that faintly tasted of orange. It was fine enough for this sort of thing, but it didn't have the zing and spice that more complex versions (those with orange peel, ginger chunks, etc.) tend to have. The Beef Rendang, an Indonesian specialty, was tasty, but it was just several chunks of beef and potato in a Rendang-flavored sauce. In better versions of this dish, the ingredients cook together for a long time to yield slightly caramelized beef and potatoes in a highly flavorful, concentrated sauce. The Thai green curry had lots of green and non-green veggies in it, but the pork was the very thinly sliced, highly processed "BBQ style" pork you find in some Chinese soups, and the green curry sauce was very thin and not very flavorful. The staff were very nice and obliging, though, and it seems to be a popular spot with some locals, so you may as well try it for yourself and see if you like it.

For the past couple years, I've been coming to Phaya Thai once every few weeks because it's a convenient stop on the way home from work, and because there aren't very many decent Thai places on the east side of town. What prompted my review tonight, however, was an experience that has has left an indelible impression on me.  I called in an order for myself and my wife (two entrees and an appetizer) and was told that it would be ready in 15 minutes.  I arrived 15 minutes later and paid, and then over the next 25 minutes, I watched a dozen orders prepared and given to people who arrived after me (after waiting 20 minutes, the polite hostess assured me that mine was next up, and three more orders went out before my food was finally ready).

This all would have been a minor inconvenience if the food had been as tasty as it normally is, but the drunken noodles were so overcooked that they had a texture that my wife likened to snot (drunken noodles are one of our favorite dishes, and these were the worst we've ever had).  The pad thai was pretty good, though, so we were at least able to split that.

I've kept my review at three stars because normally the food and service at Phaya Thai are pretty good, and you'll likely enjoy it if you like Thai food.  That said, after tonight, I think we'll drive out of the way to find a place that has more consistent quality.

My husband and I had lunch at Marnee Thai this afternoon.  It was our first and last visit. There were no carrots or onions, just grey soup with old tasting chicken, mushrooms, and small inedible pieces of lemongrass.  No garnish, either.  It tasted like watered down coconut milk with way too much fish sauce (making it way too salty).

It got worse from there.  My husband ordered the pad Thai with chicken, which he did not like.  It didn't even look appetizing. I had the cashew chicken, and it was barely edible. The chicken tasted old, like it had been cooked a week or more ago.  It might have been a tiny bit better if there had been some sauce, but there wasn't any.  Just a bit of very thin tasteless brown liquid at the bottom of the bowl.  Our meals came with small salads which were fresh but blah.  Also long thin spring rolls, about the diameter of my little finger.  They tasted good, but due to the size there was hardly any filling in them.  They came with a teeny tiny bit of dipping sauce.  We asked for more sauce, thinking we could drizzle it over our meals so they might taste a bit better.  Our server informed us that there was a 75 cent charge for each additional dipping sauce.  We don't mind in the least paying for extras when you get a decent amount. But come on, charging us for 1/2 a teaspoon of dipping sauce?

On the positive side, our server was very friendly and attentive, and the decor was pleasant.  We probably should have told our waiter how horrible our food was, but we figured since both our meals were awful and the soup was terrible, that anything else we might have ordered would be equally awful.

Don't waste your time or money eating at Marnee Thai!!

The manager never came back. 50 minutes into the wait, our waitress finally mentioned she was sorry about the wait and that the food would be out "soon." Finally, an 65 minutes after we ordered, we got our "food." My curry was a disaster. The potatoes were obviously from a can. There was little to no flavor except for bay leaf and a little spice.. and worst of all: the beef. Words can't explain how bad this "beef" was. It was completely bone dry, and actually had the texture of cardboard. You could tear it and it would crumble to pieces. It was pretty much inedible. I'm also fairly certain that the "cashews" in the curry were actually peanuts. I am a lover of Massaman curry, and this was a disgrace to the name in every way possible. Even the rice was overcooked. My girlfriend's food wasn't nearly as bad, but it still wasn't "good."

Now, I gave them a chance to redeem themselves, maybe this was just an off night. But, this is the straw that broke the camel's back. I flagged down the waitress (with a giant pile of "beef" on my plate, obviously not pleased. She never even asked me if anything was wrong with the dish, she asked me if she could do anything else. I politely (but sternly) requested that something be done since our food took SO long, and it wasn't even good when we got it. Instead of service, I got a string of lame excuses including: "If you knew anything about this restaurant, you'd know not to come right now, there's too many customers and we only have one chef." "Your dish probably got done before hers, so it sat under the heat lamp for a while." "You shouldn't come during peak hours, the waits are always long." "We have to cook from scratch, we don't use sauce from a can." "You should come back during the week when it's not so busy."
My mental response: If you can't serve this many people, then don't SEAT THIS MANY PEOPLE. Is that concept too difficult? Your sauce sure doesn't taste homemade, and even if it was... an hour for a massaman curry and a phad-thai with chicken? really?
Also, you just TOLD ME that it was put under a heat lamp. Are you stupid? You don't EVER TELL A CUSTOMER THAT.

Again, those are all mental responses. I would never berate someone in front of their clientele, even if they do deserve it.

We paid our bill and left (without tipping, they don't deserve any money for service). We'll never go back. Maybe it IS better during the week, I don't care. You don't treat a customer like that. The waitress was also spouting stuff about when "regulars" come. You won't have any new regulars if you treat customers like this.

It’s been over four years since I’ve been to Ha Long Bay – and I remember my last experience being good.  Ha Long Bay has a good reputation, but I was extremely disappointed I chose it for dinner.  I don’t know if we just were unlucky, or if things have declined, but the food was generally lackluster and flavorless.  The service was okay; our server was nice but clearly flustered…confusion with our orders being correct, not having the utensils needed to eat…it was just a generally disappointing experience.  The one good thing about it was we didn’t have to wait for a table; but maybe if we had, we would have gone somewhere else.

We started off with some appetizers, which were easily the best food items of the evening.  The Spicy Wontons were my favorite – these were the most flavorful things we tried.  They were perfectly spicy, and the bok choy was a nice touch.  The sauce was delicious.  The Thai Spring Rolls were nice, although the noodle was a little odd and floury.  I prefer the rice spring roll wrapper, but these were solid.  The fillings were good, as was the sauce.
I ordered the Green Curry with Tofu and immediately regretted it.  I had asked for a 2/5 spice, but there was no flavor to be found in this dish.  The curry was so extremely watery…this was probably the worst curry I’ve ever tried.  The sauce was more of a flavorless, thin broth.  The tofu was odd and looked like compressed, wrinkly scrambled eggs, the eggplant was almost non-existent, the bamboo was tough and chewy, and the green beans basically seemed to have come out of a freezer bag.  Maybe I just got unlucky and it was an off night for whoever made it, but I was so, so disappointed.  I ate some of it because I was hungry, but I really wish we had just ordered more appetizers and not bothered with the main dishes.

The Duck Pho was alright; the duck was a little tough and chewy for me.  The broth was alright but not as flavorful as most pho I’ve tried.  The bowl was big, but the toppings which accompanied it were a small amount.  The jalapenos were sliced too thick to eat as they were, and there weren’t many bean sprouts.

All-in-all, I would not recommend going to Ha Long Bay.  I don’t know if it was just an off night, but the experience was a far cry from the reputation they have.  As we were leaving, we saw a couple get turned away at the door because they had too long of a wait.  I was left wishing this had happened to us as well.

So I ordered Mongolian beef.  Want fried rice instead of white?  Add another couple of bucks.  In a couple of minutes, out it comes...
The few sad pieces of beef in this dish were covered by a sauce that tasted like someone put out their cigarettes in it. When I told my first-generation Mexican waiter that there wasn't very much food, he said "Thank you very much, sir."  I'm guessing he didn't understand me.
Big Bowl, big deal.  Next time I'm eating at Pei Wei.

It’s been over four years since I’ve been to Ha Long Bay – and I remember my last experience being good.  Ha Long Bay has a good reputation, but I was extremely disappointed I chose it for dinner.  I don’t know if we just were unlucky, or if things have declined, but the food was generally lackluster and flavorless.  The service was okay; our server was nice but clearly flustered…confusion with our orders being correct, not having the utensils needed to eat…it was just a generally disappointing experience.  The one good thing about it was we didn’t have to wait for a table; but maybe if we had, we would have gone somewhere else.

We started off with some appetizers, which were easily the best food items of the evening.  The Spicy Wontons were my favorite – these were the most flavorful things we tried.  They were perfectly spicy, and the bok choy was a nice touch.  The sauce was delicious.  The Thai Spring Rolls were nice, although the noodle was a little odd and floury.  I prefer the rice spring roll wrapper, but these were solid.  The fillings were good, as was the sauce.
I ordered the Green Curry with Tofu and immediately regretted it.  I had asked for a 2/5 spice, but there was no flavor to be found in this dish.  The curry was so extremely watery…this was probably the worst curry I’ve ever tried.  The sauce was more of a flavorless, thin broth.  The tofu was odd and looked like compressed, wrinkly scrambled eggs, the eggplant was almost non-existent, the bamboo was tough and chewy, and the green beans basically seemed to have come out of a freezer bag.  Maybe I just got unlucky and it was an off night for whoever made it, but I was so, so disappointed.  I ate some of it because I was hungry, but I really wish we had just ordered more appetizers and not bothered with the main dishes.

The Duck Pho was alright; the duck was a little tough and chewy for me.  The broth was alright but not as flavorful as most pho I’ve tried.  The bowl was big, but the toppings which accompanied it were a small amount.  The jalapenos were sliced too thick to eat as they were, and there weren’t many bean sprouts.

All-in-all, I would not recommend going to Ha Long Bay.  I don’t know if it was just an off night, but the experience was a far cry from the reputation they have.  As we were leaving, we saw a couple get turned away at the door because they had too long of a wait.  I was left wishing this had happened to us as well.

Usually lettuce wraps are a great suggestion to larger groups wanting to share and between six people and two kids, five people got a wrap. The rangoons, you get five for $10? At this point, I was thinking it might be better for us to agree on doing the family meal where you choose 3 apps & 3 entrees considering its $23 a person and you are for SURE exceeding that between those $30 worth of appetizers and $15+ entrees, buuuut of course people didn't want to negotiate. On that note, I ordered the make your own stirfry with the chef's choice veggies/shrimp/yellow coconut curry/Chinese noodles. I think they need more noodle options. Tried my husband's kung pow beef and yes, for sure spicy as it should be but I couldn't understand the lack of veggies for a $17 dish? I DID like the little minced up peanut bits, but otherwise, only green beans in there? Jeez. Was I comparing it to my memories of Stir Crazys kung pao? Absolutely, I had to. And yes, it's like five times better and I hardly ever ate that thing during lunch. Oh yes, let's not forget his side dish of +$1.00 fried rice. Again, lackluster, there was SOMETHING missing.

As for service, the guy was nice. We were on the patio, which I didn't initially want but it ended up being nice before the skeeters came out. I could tell by the end of our meal he was getting slowed down with the four tables around us along with ours, but he never seemed stressed or hectic and kept a good attitude. I always, always appreciate hearing "Thank you" for dining somewhere because at some places you just don't hear it anymore. Overall, great service but I was thoroughly surprised at the lack of flavors. Bill came to $196 between six adults, two kids. Alright, but again, I doubt I'd drive back there just because of what I know now. It's just not up to par and they need to knock down the prices a few dollars here and there to match the taste.

Oh! My daughter's did love their buttered noodles, so that's something.

We drive out this way quite frequently and hadn't stopped into Thai Spice before because, quite frankly we always forget to place an order before we head home. We love, love, love Thai food, however, we have several places that we are regulars at near our home.

This week we finally remembered this place while we were in the neighborhood and decided to give it a try. We ordered takeout, pad see ew, Panang Curry, and fried rice. The service was great and the food was ready on time when we arrive. We were pleased to see that they were quite busy to boot.

Once we got home things changed for the worse. The food was bad, it was however forgettable. The pad see ew had a strong smell of fermented miso or balsamic vinegar, the fried rice was bland and filled with large filler vegetables instead of rice it contained nearly half a European cucumber, strange because rice is cheap, and the curry was average.

The portions were smaller than we get from local options while costing the same, and the only reason I say that it was forgettable is that both my fiance and I literally forgot we had leftovers in the fridge, a first for Thai food.

If I lived in the area I would frequent often, the food was fine. However, it will not supplant our local options nor satisfy our cravings if we were looking for great Thai food.
Clearly states on there website that the Pad Thai is $10.50 each but when we showed up to get food the meals were $14.95. Highly unlikely we will be back.
