First and foremost, the crab cheese was very inconsistent because only two of them had an okay amount of filling (all four of them could have been more full of crab cheese filling), and when I brought this up to one of the two servers I got the response, "I watched them make it, they put a spoonful of filling in them, it's probably in the sides." This appalled me because I am the customer and I was the one who ate the food, I should know about what was in it. Word of advice: if they're not called crab rangoons, don't order them. In addition to the server not hearing my complaint, the crab cheese was also not crispy enough. Frankly, for getting 4 crab rangoons for 3.50 or something was VERY disappointing and I will never purchase them here again, that is if I even go there again.

Now for my meal, it was very good, but again, the consistency was lacking. I only had two pieces of pineapple in my dish along with a cold half ring next to the fried rice. The cold half ring helped cool the spice level, but I was very disappointed that ordering a 'pineapple curry fried rice' only netted me two pieces of pineapple in the actual dish. There were enough scallops in the dish, but the lack of pineapple really got to me and I found my self more and more disappointed as I picked through the food looking for possible pineapple chunks. Then when I asked for a take home box I got a small styrofoam container for my food which upset me as I do not support businesses who do not use acceptable take home boxes like typical Chinese food boxes or something that wasn't styrofoam, which we all know is terrible for the environment and unhealthy for humans to consume (something that is inevitable when you put hot items against the styrofoam surface causing it to melt particles into your food).

My girlfriend was very satisfied with her dish, though she had a craving for a peanut sauce Asian dish, so there's no way she could have been upset. Overall, the tasty food did not make up for the poor customer service when I had a complaint about the food I ordered. I stated that he had shown me the correct order ticket, which I had confirmed (including my name), and he had then given me the wrong bag of food. I had signed the original charge slip, and refused to give him my debit card number so that he could double-charge us.  Minutes after that call, he again called to state that they had confirmed the charge had been made, and he apologized.
IF we EVER decide to go to Yummy Bowl again, we will dine IN the restaurant to see if the experience is better.

Bangkok Thai was the absolute WORST restaurant (not only Thai) food that I've ever been to, not only the food but especially the service by the owner and waitress.
First, it took 30 minutes to get waited on, and there were only 2 people in the restaurant.  Second, I told the waitress up front that my son was allergic to nuts and fish. I asked her if any of the food we ordered (Chicken Pad Thai or Sweet and Sour Chicken) had any of these ingredients, and she said no.   We told her we had a Groupon, and she said we could use it as long as we ordered off the dinner menu..  Well my son began by eating some of the sweet n sour chicken, which had almost no chicken at all.  Maybe about 6 pieces of small inch sized chicken for a $10 entree...very very sparse. You get far more at other Thai and Chinese restaurants for less money.  Then the Chicken Pad Thai arrived. I am lucky that I took a bite first. It reeked of a strong fish smell but I took a bite to make sure . There was definitely fish in it.  I got the waitresses attention, who in a very grumpy manner came to our table.  I asked her why she told me there was no fish when there was clearly fish. I told her my son could have gotten very sick or died if he ate it. She walked away very rudely and came back 5 minutes later. She then said it has fish sauce made from fish. I told her that they need to remake this dish or give us another dish with no fish.  She then went back to the owner and they said they would refuse to remake the dish unless I paid for another entree. I was completely disgusted. Well these cheapos not only lost a great customer who eats out 2-3X a week both on business and with family, but I will make sure that I tell every website and friend I know to never visit this low class establishment again. I do feel that they would have treated me the same regardless of whether I had a coupon or not. And that shouldn't matter either way. To make a potentially life threatening mistake that could have killed my son, and not to apologize or make it right by giving us another dish and expecting us to pay for their mistake is completely outrageous.

First and foremost, the crab cheese was very inconsistent because only two of them had an okay amount of filling (all four of them could have been more full of crab cheese filling), and when I brought this up to one of the two servers I got the response, "I watched them make it, they put a spoonful of filling in them, it's probably in the sides." This appalled me because I am the customer and I was the one who ate the food, I should know about what was in it. Word of advice: if they're not called crab rangoons, don't order them. Frankly, for getting 4 crab rangoons for 3.50 or something was VERY disappointing and I will never purchase them here again, that is if I even go there again.

Now for my meal, it was very good, but again, the consistency was lacking. I only had two pieces of pineapple in my dish along with a cold half ring next to the fried rice. The cold half ring helped cool the spice level, but I was very disappointed that ordering a 'pineapple curry fried rice' only netted me two pieces of pineapple in the actual dish. There were enough scallops in the dish, but the lack of pineapple really got to me and I found my self more and more disappointed as I picked through the food looking for possible pineapple chunks. Then when I asked for a take home box I got a small styrofoam container for my food which upset me as I do not support businesses who do not use acceptable take home boxes like typical Chinese food boxes or something that wasn't styrofoam, which we all know is terrible for the environment and unhealthy for humans to consume (something that is inevitable when you put hot items against the styrofoam surface causing it to melt particles into your food).

My girlfriend was very satisfied with her dish, though she had a craving for a peanut sauce Asian dish, so there's no way she could have been upset. Overall, the tasty food did not make up for the poor customer service when I had a complaint about the food I ordered. Couple that with the inconsistency and I choose to leave this review online to express my dissatisfaction and desire to find better thai restaurants in Grand Rapids instead of Erb Thai.

(Thai Ocha - Plymouth, MI is my local standard)

Vegetables in dish:

I noticed that the vegetables didn't even look like they were sauteed in the pan. It's as if they just grabbed a handful of veggies and threw it into the dish to serve it right from the fridge. This is not how you anyone should cook their Stir Fry. Stir Fry, means you actually stir the veggies and lightly Pan Fry them to give them flavor. I'm not eating a Veggie Salad here, so don't toss in veggies straight from the fridge.

Chicken:

You should probably use a general seasoning for your poultry, because it lacked any flavor, and didn't pick up any flavor from the dish either. If you're going to pre-cook your chicken, then flavor it with something that works across the board. If not, then don't pre-cook your chicken. It seriously had no flavor at all.

Spice Level:

I expected my mouth to be somewhat on fire for ordering the second spiciest option, the Yoga Flame. Honestly, this was really mild. Taco Bell's spice packets are spicier than this, that's pretty sad that your food isn't as spicy as a fast food taco joint.

If you want to step your food game up, I suggest eating at Thai Ocha in Plymouth, MI. That's some real thai food, real flavor, real quality.

Our server dropped the check off before either of us had finished eating (she also came by multiple times during the meal to check if we were finished). I gave her my credit card to pay, which she promptly brought back (and just as promptly collected after I signed and then disappeared).
My friend and I still wanted to sit and visit, even though our server was no longer anywhere to be found and our drinks were empty (with no hope of a refill or another round in sight).  However, at 9:40 the manager on duty came by and told us we would have to leave because they were closing up.  Their posted closing is at 10.  I have been involved in the restaurant business in some capacity for nearly 20 years and this is the first (and only) time I have been asked to leave a restaurant.  Period. The fact it was well before closing borders on absurd.  I guess the manager of this place values leaving 20 minutes early to creating a welcoming atmosphere or return business.

Helpful suggestions to the staff:

1. Print new menus without white out. Go modern, less graphics, thin lines that draw the eye, and consider reducing your menu. Clean menus mean a lot and show care.
2. Get rid of the plastic water flowers. The water is a cute idea, but tacky with plastic plants. Give the guest something fresh. Orchids are elegant and easy to take care of.
3.Way too dark. Bright lights would help the dark wood and bright paint pop with out heavy Reno. Touch up the paint around the new AC units.
4.Your bathrooms are as important as your reception area. Keep them maintained.
5.Staffing is an issue. Keep ideal bodies out of the dining room and get screen printed shirts or enforce a dress code.

I was really looking forward to having a delcious Thai meal as it's one of my favorite cuisines and I have been to many places, and not limited to just Michigan. (Thai Ocha - Plymouth, MI is my local standard)

Vegetables in dish:

I noticed that the vegetables didn't even look like they were sauteed in the pan. It's as if they just grabbed a handful of veggies and threw it into the dish to serve it right from the fridge. This is not how you anyone should cook their Stir Fry. Stir Fry, means you actually stir the veggies and lightly Pan Fry them to give them flavor. I'm not eating a Veggie Salad here, so don't toss in veggies straight from the fridge.

Chicken:

You should probably use a general seasoning for your poultry, because it lacked any flavor, and didn't pick up any flavor from the dish either. If you're going to pre-cook your chicken, then flavor it with something that works across the board. If not, then don't pre-cook your chicken. It seriously had no flavor at all.

Spice Level:

I expected my mouth to be somewhat on fire for ordering the second spiciest option, the Yoga Flame. Honestly, this was really mild. Taco Bell's spice packets are spicier than this, that's pretty sad that your food isn't as spicy as a fast food taco joint.

If you want to step your food game up, I suggest eating at Thai Ocha in Plymouth, MI. That's some real thai food, real flavor, real quality.

Finally we were given the privilege of ordering, and the food took at least another 15 minutes (in itself, no big deal but we'd been there an hour by now).

Prices would be reasonable if portions were not so small. The food tasted good tho and the flavors were nice. The sauces were very flavorful. The only other issue I had with the food was that one in our party ordered Gang Pet Duck but got Curry Duck instead when the order came.

The esthetic of the restaurant was nice. It had cute date sized booths for 2 people each. There was also bar seating and family seating. The women's bathroom left something to be desired tho. It had one stall out of order, the other had a door that would not close. There was no toilet paper and it smelled unpleasant. I will not be likely to return for a second time to Soi 2.
Canned veggies,nuff said
Had high hopes as the Tao in Vegas is incredible. Tao Chicago did not come even close. Food was bland/sweet and service was ok.
The food quality was sub par compared to most Thai places in the area, and the prices were higher than they should be. The only upside is that there is a free parking lot.
I used to love this place. Went after few months with family, they were short of staff, service wasn't great. When ordered for vegetarian food, make sure you say no egg.
Fair

Food wasn't bad but it wasn't great either. Hot and sour soup was really good, general chicken was meh, mushroom soup was meh. The building and decor was really cool, neat fountains and sculptures but I feel like the place has slowly deteriorated and management hasn't noticed. Seats were all torn up and missing buttons, booth dividers are all ripped up and the ceiling vents need some serious cleaning.  The hostess was great but our server needs to take his game up a notch. We ordered sesame chicken and general chicken. When the food arrived he could not tell the difference. I tried both and they were identical, both were general chicken and neither were extra spicy as I ordered it. I brought the issue up with the sesame chicken with the waiter, he took the plate away and brought it back a few moments later with the same general chicken on it but this time with sesame seeds on It!  On what planet is general chicken and sesame chicken only differentiated by the absence of sesame seeds??? Super lazy attempt by the waiter and/or cook.

I will come back and give it another chance at dinner time but I do not have high hopes.
Not terrible food, but not very good. Ordered food for pick up, took 50 minutes. Not really worth it, particularly at the price point.

We ordered two entrees and a soup. The server brought out the entrees right before the soup..?! Staff were nice but it took us an hour to get our sushi. Take out would have been faster.

Quality of food isn't what it used to be.  Missing a lot of flavor and a lot of love.  It's sad because I used to love this place.
Good, but expensive. Paid a lot for very little food.

Loved it, will come back again to try more items on the menu!
Edit: Tried it again on 5/11/19, very disappointed. Have tried 8 different dishes so far and have to say the majority of them were overseasoned. Maybe the majority of white folk just like it that way, and the restaurant is trying to appeal to its clients.

However, the cook needs to learn how to make rice. The rice I got was mushy and soggy. It's inexcusable, embarrassing. The rice was more like congee/oatmeal than steamed rice. Rice is one of the most basic and important ingredients in Asian cooking and if you can't get something so simple right, that casts a shadow on everything else that comes out of the kitchen. I recommend investing in a quality rice cooker.

Ordered spicy shrimp maki roll and pad thai.  Roll was okay, something that you could get from any grocery store.  Pad thai was horrible. Taste was okay, but all the noodles were chopped up into about 1/2 inch.  It was very unappetizing and when I asked waitress if it was supposed to be, she told me maybe it got shorter while I was eating...seriously? I would've been okay if she just told me they used left over noodle than give me some bs excuse. Thai ice tea was not that good either.  Over all, I was bit disappointed.

Thought this was a restaurant opened for lunch. It was difficult to get anything to drink after we sat down. They had tea bags you could use with hot water and Styrofoam cups. If you wanted anything else to drink there was a cooler with canned drinks to choose from. Then we had to wait as they were busy filling take out orders. Once the food arrived it was fair.

Very clean and very friendly with some seating. With that said: Not impressed. I was excited to try Panda Garden after all the rave reviews and being so close. I am disappointed in the food and the severing sizes after the reviews. It is expensive for what you get. Those who say the portions are huge must not visit other Chinese restaurants in the area. The almond gravy tasted like garlic and not much else. The rice also lacks in flavor. The egg roll was ok. The wonton soup is good though (rreason I gave 3 stars and not 2). It is not the worst Almond Chicken I have had but not the best either. I most likely will be going only for wonton soup when I am not feeling good (like today) it was good and priced according to others in the area.

To the owners response:
Other local places charge $7-8 for their DINNERS with triple the food that you gave for the lunch portion and it is what Almond Chicken should taste like
